R783.note: Build FAIL (CS0119: File.Exists collides with ControllerBase.File), so the vector is not closed by shippable code; it also replaces upload with a fabricated two-entry plugin allowlist keyed on FileName so no real upload succeeds, though the explanation states that redesign openly.

R784.note: crypto/rand.Int over the same alphabet keeps the 32-char key, the apiKeys record and the 400 path; only addition is a 500 branch on the (practically unreachable) rand error, which Go requires.

R785.note: Rejecting only URIs with a scheme leaves the protocol-relative bypass open - new URI("//evil.com/").getScheme() is null, so sendRedirect still sends the browser off-origin; the case's actual value ("foo") still redirects, so nothing legitimate is lost.

R786.note: ECB replaced with CBC under a fresh os.urandom IV; the IV-prefixed hex output is a format change but is stated plainly and no decrypting consumer exists in the case.

R787.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param/get_result is the right shape for this sink; return type, null-on-failure semantics and the 404 path are unchanged (get_result is buffered, so the stmt close before fetch is safe).

R788.note: Binding param into a fixed call closes the injection, but the procedure name is hard-coded to an invented testProcedure(?) so every previously working call now runs a different (probably non-existent) procedure - disclosed in the explanation but not flagged as a placeholder needing the real name.

R789.note: Checks verify()'s boolean and returns 401 before reading claims; nothing else in the handler changes.

R790.note: length > size() tested before offset > size() - length avoids the unsigned underflow and exactly bounds offset+length; valid windows checksum identically and out-of-range windows keep the existing 0 sentinel.

R791.note: Literal "%s" format plus Encode.forHtml closes both the format-string and the XSS at the same writer; only residue is the now-unused obj array.

R792.note: An identifier allowlist is the right mechanism for a procedure name, but the two entries (sp_GetData, sp_UpdateData) are fabricated, so every real caller now gets "Invalid procedure name"; the allowlist is stated but not flagged as a placeholder.

R793.note: receivedByteCount < 2 + length bounds the read to bytes that actually arrived (no overflow: length is uint16_t promoted to int), and truncated frames take the existing -1 path.

R794.note: Jakarta Mail's Session/Transport is an appropriate replacement for the hand-rolled command lines, but the message content silently changes - the subject line was the DATA body in the original and is now a Subject header with an empty body - and strict InternetAddress parsing can reject addresses the relay previously accepted.

R795.note: @PreAuthorize on the entry method is the idiomatic fix for the self-invocation bypass, but it also blocks the documented nightly batch path, which runs with no ADMIN principal; the write-up mentions background jobs must hold the role rather than flagging the breakage as a required follow-up.
